{"id": "58:4", "fails": ["native", "plain"], "remarks": [{"words": "Porque eis que apanharam a minha alma", "problem": "'apanharam' is colloquial in Brazil (to catch a bus, to take a beating); it lowers the register exactly where the soul is seized, and 'eis que apanharam' is a small tongue-trip.", "alternative": "Porque eis que prenderam a minha alma: * lançaram-se sobre mim os fortes."}]},
{"id": "58:5", "fails": ["native"], "remarks": [{"words": "e segui direito", "problem": "'segui direito' sounds like street directions ('go straight on'); the ear hears traffic, not moral uprightness.", "alternative": "sem iniquidade corri, e segui reto."}]},
{"id": "58:6b", "fails": ["native", "sayable"], "remarks": [{"words": "Atendei, para visitar todas as nações", "problem": "'Atendei' standing alone and then 'para visitar' reads as a purpose clause bolted on; the Latin's 'be intent on visiting' is lost and the comma makes an unnatural pause after the first word.", "alternative": "Aplicai-vos a visitar todas as nações: * não tenhais piedade de todos os que praticam a iniquidade."}]},
{"id": "58:7", "fails": ["noRhyme"], "remarks": [{"words": "Voltarão ... passarão fome como cães, * e rodearão", "problem": "Four nasal -ão/-ães beats in one short verse (voltarão, passarão, cães, rodearão); the mediant 'cães' chimes with both futures. The futures are unavoidable, but the middle one can be moved off the stress.", "alternative": "Voltarão à tarde, e como cães terão fome, * e rodearão a cidade."}]},
{"id": "58:10", "fails": ["sayable", "native"], "remarks": [{"words": "porque vós sois, Deus, o meu amparo", "problem": "The vocative wedged between verb and predicate ('sois, Deus, o') makes the reader stop twice in three words; it stutters in choir.", "alternative": "porque vós, ó Deus, sois o meu amparo"}, {"words": "a sua misericórdia se adiantará a mim", "problem": "'se adiantará a mim' is awkward and faintly bureaucratic ('will get ahead of me'); the final cadence falls on a limp 'a mim'.", "alternative": "meu Deus, a sua misericórdia me precederá."}]},
{"id": "58:12", "fails": ["native"], "remarks": [{"words": "para que não se esqueçam do meu povo", "problem": "Beyond the ear: this makes 'my people' the thing forgotten, whereas 'nequándo obliviscántur pópuli mei' most naturally has my people(s) as the ones who forget; the Portuguese quietly resolves (or shifts) the Latin. Also 'se esqueçam do' is looser than needed.", "alternative": "para que o meu povo nunca se esqueça."}]},
{"id": "58:13", "fails": ["plain"], "remarks": [{"words": "A falta da sua boca", "problem": "'falta' is first heard as 'lack, absence', not 'offence'; the listener must reinterpret.", "alternative": "O delito da sua boca, a palavra dos seus lábios: * e sejam presos na sua soberba."}]},
{"id": "58:13b", "fails": ["noRhyme", "sayable", "concrete"], "remarks": [{"words": "na consumação: * ... e deixarão de existir", "problem": "Mediant 'consumação' rhymes with 'deixarão' in the final colon; 'deixarão de existir' is also an abstract, clinical paraphrase of the stark 'non erunt'. "overall": "The psalm mostly sounds plain and sober, with a good austere line in the cries of 2–3 and the closing thanksgiving; it follows the Latin faithfully without sounding stilted most of the time. It falters where colloquial verbs slip in (apanharam, segui direito), in the vocative stutter 'sois, Deus, o' of the refrain verses 10 and 18, and in the obscure, rhyme-marred 13b.",
"worstLine": "58:13b",
